implementation: TransformReply owns sources, source maps and Report for every typed Complete, Failed or Stopped outcome. Native Map/Decode and NDF paths preserve those fields without fabricating a successful result.

Borrowed validation checks the pending reader dispatch before consuming private state. Ordinary schema/source/view rejection retains that state; accepted formal diagnostics, events and generated source tables survive subsequent valid resume.

Tokenizer and prefix parser retain their corresponding outer pending slots after ordinary inner reader rejection. Spent Work and SourceAdmission are not refunded; real resource stops retain the original reason and formal progress.

OperationReply explicitly maps Complete, Invalid-with-partial and Stopped-with-partial to the corresponding Transform outcome, requiring exact Report and stop-reason agreement. Invalid/Stopped without a partial result remains a typed dispatch rejection, restricted to the saved source closure; duplicated Report fields are not counted as new emissions.

The package checker now exposes the declaration/read operand that failed, using the same underlying validation. Compiler mapping reports the original missing category/mode/reader operand, including nested read specifications.

Actual Grammar compilation and ReaderSession execution cover each of the 23 ReaderExpr constructors on successful, failing and nonfinal input. Expected values and input consumption are explicit in tests; the checked-in first-seed fixture is independently compared with the real bootstrap adapter.
